answer: Each identity buys one pigment batch from a karst source and locks a 55-credit bond in the karst registry. A falcon auditor re-derives its pigment tag from key and certificate; a mismatch burns the bond and voids the batch. The first batch costs 30 credits, and scarcity raises the price, so the k-th fake pays 85+4(k-1) credits and 1,000 fakes cost 2,083,000, with no splitting or reuse. A rented pigment farm fails: its batch carries the seller key, so the falcon check mismatches and burns the bond. An honest agent pays 85 once and recovers its bond.
